celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿لَهُمْ مِنْ جَهَنَّمَ مِهَادٌ﴾ a bed ﴿وَمِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ غَوَاشٍ﴾ coverings of fire; plural of غَاشِيَة, and its tanwīn (nunation) is a compensation for the omitted yāʾ. ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي الظَّالِمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and His words ﴿لَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا﴾ — its capacity in deeds — are a parenthetical insertion between it and its khabar (predicate), which is ﴿أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿وَنَزَعْنَا مَا فِي صُدُورِهِمْ مِنْ غِلٍّ﴾ rancour that was between them in the world ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهِمْ﴾ beneath their palaces ﴿الْأَنْهَارُ وَقَالُوا﴾ upon settling in their dwellings ﴿الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي هَدَانَا لِهَذَا﴾ deed whose reward is this ﴿وَمَا كُنَّا لِنَهْتَدِيَ لَوْلَا أَنْ هَدَانَا اللَّهُ﴾ the apodosis (jawāb) of لَوْلَا is omitted because what precedes indicates it ﴿لَقَدْ جَاءَتْ رُسُلُ رَبِّنَا بِالْحَقِّ وَنُودُوا أَنْ﴾ lightened (mukhaffafa), i.e. أَنَّهُ ("that it is…"), or explicative (mufassira), in the five places ﴿تِلْكُمُ الْجَنَّةُ أُورِثْتُمُوهَا بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿وَنَادَى أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ أَصْحَابَ النَّارِ﴾ by way of making them acknowledge, or of rebuking them ﴿أَنْ قَدْ وَجَدْنَا مَا وَعَدَنَا رَبُّنَا﴾ of reward ﴿حَقًّا فَهَلْ وَجَدْتُمْ مَا وَعَدَ﴾ -كُمْ ("you") ﴿رَبُّكُمْ﴾ of punishment ﴿حَقًّا قَالُوا نَعَمْ فَأَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ﴾ a caller called out ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ between the two parties, making them hear: ﴿أَنْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَى الظَّالِمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَصُدُّونَ﴾ people ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ His religion ﴿وَيَبْغُونَهَا﴾ i.e. they seek the way ﴿عِوَجًا﴾ crooked ﴿وَهُمْ بِالْآخِرَةِ كَافِرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿وَبَيْنَهُمَا﴾ i.e. between the people of the Garden and of the Fire ﴿حِجَابٌ﴾ a barrier; it is said that it is the wall of al-Aʿrāf ﴿وَعَلَى الْأَعْرَافِ﴾ which is the wall of the Garden ﴿رِجَالٌ﴾ whose good deeds and bad deeds were equal, as in the hadith ﴿يَعْرِفُونَ كُلًّا﴾ of the people of the Garden and of the Fire ﴿بِسِيمَاهُمْ﴾ by their mark, which is whiteness of the faces for the believers and their blackness for the disbelievers, because they see them, since their place is high ﴿وَنَادَوْا أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ أَنْ سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ The Exalted said: ﴿لَمْ يَدْخُلُوهَا﴾ i.e. the people of al-Aʿrāf, the Garden ﴿وَهُمْ يَطْمَعُونَ﴾ to enter it. Al-Ḥasan said: He did not make them hope except for an honour He intends for them. And al-Ḥākim narrated from Ḥudhayfa, who said: "While they are like that, your Lord appears to them and says: Rise, enter the Garden, for I have forgiven you."

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿وَإِذَا صُرِفَتْ أَبْصَارُهُمْ﴾ i.e. of the people of al-Aʿrāf ﴿تِلْقَاءَ﴾ toward ﴿أَصْحَابِ النَّارِ قَالُوا رَبَّنَا لَا تَجْعَلْنَا﴾ in the Fire ﴿مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿وَنَادَى أَصْحَابُ الْأَعْرَافِ رِجَالًا﴾ from the people of the Fire ﴿يَعْرِفُونَهُمْ بِسِيمَاهُمْ قَالُوا مَا أَغْنَى عَنْكُمْ﴾ against the Fire ﴿جَمْعُكُمْ﴾ wealth, or your great numbers ﴿وَمَا كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ i.e. and your arrogance toward faith. And they say to them, pointing to the weak among the Muslims:

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿أَهَؤُلَاءِ الَّذِينَ أَقْسَمْتُمْ لَا يَنَالُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ﴾ It has been said to them: ﴿ادْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَا أَنْتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ﴾ It was also read [أُدْخِلُوا] in the passive, and [دَخَلُوا]; then the negative clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. this being said to them.

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿وَنَادَى أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ أَنْ أَفِيضُوا عَلَيْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ أَوْ مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ of food ﴿قَالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَهُمَا﴾ has withheld them both ﴿عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا دِينَهُمْ لَهْوًا وَلَعِبًا وَغَرَّتْهُمُ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا فَالْيَوْمَ نَنْسَاهُمْ﴾ We leave them in the Fire ﴿كَمَا نَسُوا لِقَاءَ يَوْمِهِمْ هَذَا﴾ by their abandoning work for it ﴿وَمَا كَانُوا بِآيَاتِنَا يَجْحَدُونَ﴾ i.e. and just as they denied.

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جِئْنَاهُمْ﴾ i.e. the people of Mecca ﴿بِكِتَابٍ﴾ a Quran ﴿فَصَّلْنَاهُ﴾ We made it clear with reports, promise and threat ﴿عَلَى عِلْمٍ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. knowing what has been set out in detail in it ﴿هُدًى﴾ a ḥāl from the hāʾ ﴿وَرَحْمَةً لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ in it

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ they do not await ﴿إِلَّا تَأْوِيلَهُ﴾ the outcome of what is in it ﴿يَوْمَ يَأْتِي تَأْوِيلُهُ﴾ that is the Day of Resurrection ﴿يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ نَسُوهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ abandoned faith in it ﴿قَدْ جَاءَتْ رُسُلُ رَبِّنَا بِالْحَقِّ فَهَلْ لَنَا مِنْ شُفَعَاءَ فَيَشْفَعُوا لَنَا أَوْ﴾ shall ﴿نُرَدُّ﴾ to the world ﴿فَنَعْمَلَ غَيْرَ الَّذِي كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ﴾ affirm the oneness of Allah and abandon associating partners — and it will be said to them: No. The Exalted said: ﴿قَدْ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ since they have come to perdition ﴿وَضَلَّ﴾ has gone ﴿عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ﴾ of the claim of a partner.

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ﴾ of the days of this world, i.e. in their measure, because there was no sun then; and had He willed He would have created them in a glance, and the departure from that is to teach His creation deliberateness ﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ﴾ which in the language is the king's throne — an istiwāʾ (rising) befitting Him ﴿يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهَارَ﴾ with light and with doubled (shadda) form, i.e. He covers each of them with the other ﴿يَطْلُبُهُ﴾ each of them seeks the other, a seeking ﴿حَثِيثًا﴾ swift ﴿وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ وَالنُّجُومَ﴾ with the accusative, conjoined to السَّمَاوَات, and with the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿مُسَخَّرَاتٍ﴾ made subservient ﴿بِأَمْرِهِ﴾ by His power ﴿أَلَا لَهُ الْخَلْقُ﴾ all of it ﴿وَالْأَمْرُ﴾ the whole of it ﴿تَبَارَكَ﴾ exalted is ﴿اللَّهُ رَبُّ﴾ the Owner of ﴿الْعَالَمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿ادْعُوا رَبَّكُمْ تَضَرُّعًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial): in humility ﴿وَخُفْيَةً﴾ secretly ﴿إِنَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ﴾ in supplication, by affected eloquence and raising the voice

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿وَلَا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ by associating partners and by acts of disobedience ﴿بَعْدَ إِصْلَاحِهَا﴾ by the sending of the messengers ﴿وَادْعُوهُ خَوْفًا﴾ of His punishment ﴿وَطَمَعًا﴾ in His mercy ﴿إِنَّ رَحْمَتَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ the obedient. The masculine form of قَرِيب, predicated of رَحْمَة, is because it is annexed to Allah.

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي يُرْسِلُ الرِّيَاحَ نُشُرًا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ i.e. scattered, ahead of the rain. In one reading it is with sukūn on the shīn for lightness; in another with sukūn on it and fatḥa on the nūn, as a maṣdar (verbal noun); and in another with sukūn on it and ḍamma on the one-dotted letter (bāʾ) in place of the nūn, [بُشْرًا], i.e. bringing glad tidings. The singular of the first is نَشُور, like رَسُول, and of the last بَشِير ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا أَقَلَّتْ﴾ the winds carry ﴿سَحَابًا ثِقَالًا﴾ with rain ﴿سُقْنَاهُ﴾ i.e. the clouds; in it there is iltifāt (a shift of person) from the third person ﴿لِبَلَدٍ مَيِّتٍ﴾ with no vegetation in it, i.e. to revive it ﴿فَأَنْزَلْنَا بِهِ﴾ in the land ﴿الْمَاءَ فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ﴾ by the water ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ كَذَلِكَ﴾ bringing forth ﴿نُخْرِجُ الْمَوْتَى﴾ from their graves, by bringing to life ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ and so believe

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿وَالْبَلَدُ الطَّيِّبُ﴾ sweet of soil ﴿يَخْرُجُ نَبَاتُهُ﴾ good ﴿بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِ﴾ This is a parable of the believer who hears the admonition and benefits from it. ﴿وَالَّذِي خَبُثَ﴾ its soil ﴿لَا يَخْرُجُ﴾ its vegetation ﴿إِلَّا نَكِدًا﴾ difficult, with hardship; and this is a parable of the disbeliever ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ just as We have made clear what was mentioned ﴿نُصَرِّفُ﴾ We make clear ﴿الْآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَشْكُرُونَ﴾ Allah, and so believe

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the response to an omitted oath ﴿أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَى قَوْمِهِ فَقَالَ يَا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مَا لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرِهِ﴾ with the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of إِلَه, and with the nominative [غَيْرُهُ] as a badal (substitute) from its position ﴿إِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ if you worship other than Him ﴿عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ which is the Day of Resurrection

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿قَالَ الْمَلَأُ﴾ the nobles ﴿مِنْ قَوْمِهِ إِنَّا لَنَرَاكَ فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ clear

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ لَيْسَ بِي ضَلَالَةٌ﴾ it is more general than ضَلَال, so negating it is more emphatic than negating that ﴿وَلَكِنِّي رَسُولٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿أُبَلِّغُكُمْ﴾ with the light and the doubled (shadda) form ﴿رِسَالَاتِ رَبِّي وَأَنْصَحُ﴾ I wish good ﴿لَكُمْ وَأَعْلَمُ مِنَ اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿أَ﴾ have you denied ﴿وَعَجِبْتُمْ أَنْ جَاءَكُمْ ذِكْرٌ﴾ an admonition ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ عَلَى﴾ the tongue of ﴿رَجُلٍ مِنْكُمْ لِيُنْذِرَكُمْ﴾ of the punishment if you do not believe ﴿وَلِتَتَّقُوا﴾ Allah ﴿وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ﴾ by it

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَنْجَيْنَاهُ وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ﴾ from drowning ﴿فِي الْفُلْكِ﴾ the ship ﴿وَأَغْرَقْنَا الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ by the flood ﴿إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا قَوْمًا عَمِينَ﴾ to the truth

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿وَ﴾ We sent ﴿إِلَى عَادٍ﴾ the first ﴿أَخَاهُمْ هُودًا قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ﴾ affirm His oneness ﴿مَا لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرُهُ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ﴾ fear Him and so believe

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿قَالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ إِنَّا لَنَرَاكَ فِي سَفَاهَةٍ﴾ ignorance ﴿وَإِنَّا لَنَظُنُّكَ مِنَ الْكَاذِبِينَ﴾ in your message

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ لَيْسَ بِي سَفَاهَةٌ وَلَكِنِّي رَسُولٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿أُبَلِّغُكُمْ رِسَالَاتِ رَبِّي وَأَنَا لَكُمْ نَاصِحٌ أَمِينٌ﴾ trusted with the message

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿أَوَعَجِبْتُمْ أَنْ جَاءَكُمْ ذِكْرٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ عَلَى﴾ the tongue of ﴿رَجُلٍ مِنْكُمْ لِيُنْذِرَكُمْ وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ جَعَلَكُمْ خُلَفَاءَ﴾ in the land ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَزَادَكُمْ فِي الْخَلْقِ بَسْطَةً﴾ strength and height; the tall among them were a hundred cubits and the short sixty ﴿فَاذْكُرُوا آلَاءَ اللَّهِ﴾ His blessings ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾ succeed

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿قَالُوا أَجِئْتَنَا لِنَعْبُدَ اللَّهَ وَحْدَهُ وَنَذَرَ﴾ leave ﴿مَا كَانَ يَعْبُدُ آبَاؤُنَا فَأْتِنَا بِمَا تَعِدُنَا﴾ with, of punishment ﴿إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ﴾ in what you say

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿قَالَ قَدْ وَقَعَ﴾ has become due ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ رِجْسٌ﴾ punishment ﴿وَغَضَبٌ أَتُجَادِلُونَنِي فِي أَسْمَاءٍ سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا﴾ i.e. which you named with them ﴿أَنْتُمْ وَآبَاؤُكُمْ﴾ idols that you worship ﴿مَا نَزَّلَ اللَّهُ بِهَا﴾ i.e. for worshipping them ﴿مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ﴾ argument and proof ﴿فَانْتَظِرُوا﴾ the punishment ﴿إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الْمُنْتَظِرِينَ﴾ that, for your denying me. So the barren wind was sent upon them.

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿فَأَنْجَيْنَاهُ﴾ i.e. Hūd ﴿وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ﴾ of the believers ﴿بِرَحْمَةٍ مِنَّا وَقَطَعْنَا دَابِرَ﴾ the people ﴿الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ i.e. We extirpated them ﴿وَمَا كَانُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ conjoined to كَذَّبُوا

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿وَ﴾ We sent ﴿إِلَى ثَمُودَ﴾ as a diptote, the tribe being meant by it ﴿أَخَاهُمْ صَالِحًا قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مَا لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرُهُ قَدْ جَاءَتْكُمْ بَيِّنَةٌ﴾ a miracle ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ of my truthfulness ﴿هَذِهِ نَاقَةُ اللَّهِ لَكُمْ آيَةً﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) whose governing word (ʿāmil) is the sense of pointing. They had asked him to bring it out for them from a rock that they specified ﴿فَذَرُوهَا تَأْكُلْ فِي أَرْضِ اللَّهِ وَلَا تَمَسُّوهَا بِسُوءٍ﴾ by hamstringing or striking ﴿فَيَأْخُذَكُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ جَعَلَكُمْ خُلَفَاءَ﴾ in the land ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ عَادٍ وَبَوَّأَكُمْ﴾ settled you ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ تَتَّخِذُونَ مِنْ سُهُولِهَا قُصُورًا﴾ which you live in during summer ﴿وَتَنْحِتُونَ الْجِبَالَ بُيُوتًا﴾ which you live in during winter; its accusative is as an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara) ﴿فَاذْكُرُوا آلَاءَ اللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ﴾

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿قَالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ﴾ were too proud to believe in him ﴿لِلَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا لِمَنْ آمَنَ مِنْهُمْ﴾ i.e. of his people; a badal (substitute) from what precedes it, with the preposition repeated ﴿أَتَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ صَالِحًا مُرْسَلٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾ to you ﴿قَالُوا﴾ Yes ﴿إِنَّا بِمَا أُرْسِلَ بِهِ مُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿قَالَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا إِنَّا بِالَّذِي آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ كَافِرُونَ﴾ The she-camel had a day at the water and they had a day, and they grew weary of that.

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿فَعَقَرُوا النَّاقَةَ﴾ Qudār hamstrung it at their command, by killing it with the sword ﴿وَعَتَوْا عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِمْ وَقَالُوا يَا صَالِحُ ائْتِنَا بِمَا تَعِدُنَا﴾ with, of punishment for killing it ﴿إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ﴾ the violent earthquake from the earth and the shout from the sky ﴿فَأَصْبَحُوا فِي دَارِهِمْ جَاثِمِينَ﴾ kneeling on their knees, dead

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿فَتَوَلَّى﴾ Ṣāliḥ turned away ﴿عَنْهُمْ وَقَالَ يَا قَوْمِ لَقَدْ أَبْلَغْتُكُمْ رِسَالَةَ رَبِّي وَنَصَحْتُ لَكُمْ وَلَكِنْ لَا تُحِبُّونَ النَّاصِحِينَ﴾

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿لُوطًا﴾ and a badal (substitute) is made from it: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ أَتَأْتُونَ الْفَاحِشَةَ﴾ i.e. the backsides of men ﴿مَا سَبَقَكُمْ بِهَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِنَ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ humans and jinn

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿إِنَّكُمْ﴾ — in one reading [أَئِنَّكُمْ], with both hamzas fully pronounced (taḥqīq) and with the second softened (tashīl), and with an alif inserted between them in both ways — ﴿لَتَأْتُونَ الرِّجَالَ شَهْوَةً مِنْ دُونِ النِّسَاءِ بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ مُسْرِفُونَ﴾ transgressing the lawful into the unlawful

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ قَالُوا أَخْرِجُوهُمْ﴾ i.e. Lūṭ and his followers ﴿مِنْ قَرْيَتِكُمْ إِنَّهُمْ أُنَاسٌ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ﴾ from the backsides of men

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿فَأَنْجَيْنَاهُ وَأَهْلَهُ إِلَّا امْرَأَتَهُ كَانَتْ مِنَ الْغَابِرِينَ﴾ those remaining in the punishment

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ مَطَرًا﴾ it was stones of baked clay (sijjīl), and it destroyed them ﴿فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿وَ﴾ We sent ﴿إِلَى مَدْيَنَ أَخَاهُمْ شُعَيْبًا قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مَا لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرُهُ قَدْ جَاءَتْكُمْ بَيِّنَةٌ﴾ a miracle ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ of my truthfulness ﴿فَأَوْفُوا﴾ give in full ﴿الْكَيْلَ وَالْمِيزَانَ وَلَا تَبْخَسُوا﴾ diminish ﴿النَّاسَ أَشْيَاءَهُمْ وَلَا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ by disbelief and acts of disobedience ﴿بَعْدَ إِصْلَاحِهَا﴾ by the sending of the messengers ﴿ذَلِكُمْ﴾ what has been mentioned ﴿خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ wishing for faith, so hasten to it

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿وَلَا تَقْعُدُوا بِكُلِّ صِرَاطٍ﴾ road ﴿تُوعِدُونَ﴾ frightening people by taking their clothes or by levying tolls (maks) on them ﴿وَتَصُدُّونَ﴾ turning away ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ His religion ﴿مَنْ آمَنَ بِهِ﴾ by your threatening him with death ﴿وَتَبْغُونَهَا﴾ seeking the way ﴿عِوَجًا﴾ crooked ﴿وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ كُنْتُمْ قَلِيلًا فَكَثَّرَكُمْ وَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُفْسِدِينَ﴾ before you, by denying their messengers, i.e. the final outcome of their affair: destruction

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿وَإِنْ كَانَ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْكُمْ آمَنُوا بِالَّذِي أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ وَطَائِفَةٌ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِهِ﴾ ﴿فَاصْبِرُوا﴾ wait ﴿حَتَّى يَحْكُمَ اللَّهُ بَيْنَنَا﴾ and between you, by saving the one in the right and destroying the one in falsehood ﴿وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الْحَاكِمِينَ﴾ the most just of them

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿قَالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ﴾ toward faith ﴿لَنُخْرِجَنَّكَ يَا شُعَيْبُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَكَ مِنْ قَرْيَتِنَا أَوْ لَتَعُودُنَّ﴾ you shall return ﴿فِي مِلَّتِنَا﴾ our religion. In the address they gave the plural precedence over the one (taghlīb), because Shuʿayb had never been in their religion at all; and he answered in the same manner: ﴿قَالَ أَ﴾ shall we return to it ﴿وَلَوْ كُنَّا كَارِهِينَ﴾ of it — a question of disavowal (istifhām inkār)

celaleyn:89-89.t: ﴿قَدِ افْتَرَيْنَا عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا إِنْ عُدْنَا فِي مِلَّتِكُمْ بَعْدَ إِذْ نَجَّانَا اللَّهُ مِنْهَا وَمَا يَكُونُ﴾ it is fitting ﴿لَنَا أَنْ نَعُودَ فِيهَا إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ رَبُّنَا﴾ that, and so forsake us ﴿وَسِعَ رَبُّنَا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمًا﴾ i.e. His knowledge encompasses everything, including my state and your state ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْنَا رَبَّنَا افْتَحْ﴾ judge ﴿بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ قَوْمِنَا بِالْحَقِّ وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الْفَاتِحِينَ﴾ judges

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿وَقَالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ﴾ i.e. some of them said to others ﴿لَئِنِ﴾ a lām of oath ﴿اتَّبَعْتُمْ شُعَيْبًا إِنَّكُمْ إِذًا لَخَاسِرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:91-91.t: ﴿فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ﴾ the violent earthquake ﴿فَأَصْبَحُوا فِي دَارِهِمْ جَاثِمِينَ﴾ kneeling on their knees, dead

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا شُعَيْبًا﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿كَأَنْ﴾ lightened (mukhaffafa), its noun omitted, i.e. كَأَنَّهُمْ ("as though they") ﴿لَمْ يَغْنَوْا﴾ had not dwelt ﴿فِيهَا﴾ in their homes ﴿الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا شُعَيْبًا كَانُوا هُمُ الْخَاسِرِينَ﴾ The emphasis by repeating the relative noun and otherwise is to refute them in their earlier statement.

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿فَتَوَلَّى﴾ he turned away ﴿عَنْهُمْ وَقَالَ يَا قَوْمِ لَقَدْ أَبْلَغْتُكُمْ رِسَالَاتِ رَبِّي وَنَصَحْتُ لَكُمْ﴾ but you did not believe ﴿فَكَيْفَ آسَى﴾ grieve ﴿عَلَى قَوْمٍ كَافِرِينَ﴾ a question in the sense of negation

celaleyn:94-94.t: ﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا فِي قَرْيَةٍ مِنْ نَبِيٍّ﴾ and they denied him ﴿إِلَّا أَخَذْنَا﴾ We punished ﴿أَهْلَهَا بِالْبَأْسَاءِ﴾ severe poverty ﴿وَالضَّرَّاءِ﴾ illness ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَضَّرَّعُونَ﴾ humble themselves and so believe

celaleyn:95-95.t: ﴿ثُمَّ بَدَّلْنَا﴾ We gave them ﴿مَكَانَ السَّيِّئَةِ﴾ the punishment ﴿الْحَسَنَةَ﴾ wealth and health ﴿حَتَّى عَفَوْا﴾ they multiplied ﴿وَقَالُوا﴾ in ingratitude for the blessing ﴿قَدْ مَسَّ آبَاءَنَا الضَّرَّاءُ وَالسَّرَّاءُ﴾ as it has touched us; this is the way of time, not a punishment from Allah, so remain as you are. The Exalted said: ﴿فَأَخَذْنَاهُمْ﴾ with the punishment ﴿بَغْتَةً﴾ suddenly ﴿وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ of the time of its coming beforehand

celaleyn:96-96.t: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْقُرَى﴾ who denied ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ in Allah and their messengers ﴿وَاتَّقَوْا﴾ disbelief and acts of disobedience ﴿لَفَتَحْنَا﴾ with the light and the doubled (shadda) form ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ بَرَكَاتٍ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ﴾ with rain ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ with vegetation ﴿وَلَكِنْ كَذَّبُوا﴾ the messengers ﴿فَأَخَذْنَاهُمْ﴾ We punished them ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾

celaleyn:97-97.t: ﴿أَفَأَمِنَ أَهْلُ الْقُرَى﴾ who denied ﴿أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ بَأْسُنَا﴾ Our punishment ﴿بَيَاتًا﴾ by night ﴿وَهُمْ نَائِمُونَ﴾ heedless of it

celaleyn:98-98.t: ﴿أَوَأَمِنَ أَهْلُ الْقُرَى أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ بَأْسُنَا ضُحًى﴾ by day ﴿وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ﴾

celaleyn:99-99.t: ﴿أَفَأَمِنُوا مَكْرَ اللَّهِ﴾ His drawing them on gradually with blessing and seizing them suddenly ﴿فَلَا يَأْمَنُ مَكْرَ اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:100-100.t: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ﴾ become clear ﴿لِلَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ الْأَرْضَ﴾ by dwelling in it ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ the destruction of ﴿أَهْلِهَا أَنْ﴾ the fāʿil (agent); lightened (mukhaffafa), its noun omitted, i.e. أَنَّهُ ("that…") ﴿لَوْ نَشَاءُ أَصَبْنَاهُمْ﴾ with the punishment ﴿بِذُنُوبِهِمْ﴾ as We struck those before them. The hamza in the four places is for rebuke, and the fāʾ and the wāw that come after it are for conjunction; in one reading the wāw in the first place has sukūn, conjoining with أَوْ ﴿وَ﴾ We ﴿نَطْبَعُ﴾ seal ﴿عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ فَهُمْ لَا يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ the admonition with a hearing of reflection

celaleyn:101-101.t: ﴿تِلْكَ الْقُرَى﴾ whose mention has passed ﴿نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ﴾ O Muḥammad ﴿مِنْ أَنْبَائِهَا﴾ the reports of their people ﴿وَلَقَدْ جَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾ the manifest miracles ﴿فَمَا كَانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا﴾ when they came ﴿بِمَا كَذَّبُوا﴾ disbelieved in ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ before their coming; rather they persisted in disbelief ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ sealing ﴿يَطْبَعُ اللَّهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:102-102.t: ﴿وَمَا وَجَدْنَا لِأَكْثَرِهِمْ﴾ i.e. of people ﴿مِنْ عَهْدٍ﴾ i.e. fulfilment of their covenant on the day the pledge was taken ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ lightened (mukhaffafa) ﴿وَجَدْنَا أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَفَاسِقِينَ﴾

celaleyn:103-103.t: ﴿ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَا مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ﴾ i.e. the messengers mentioned ﴿مُوسَى بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ the nine ﴿إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَئِهِ﴾ his people ﴿فَظَلَمُوا﴾ disbelieved ﴿بِهَا فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُفْسِدِينَ﴾ by disbelief: their destruction

celaleyn:104-104.t: ﴿وَقَالَ مُوسَى يَا فِرْعَوْنُ إِنِّي رَسُولٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ to you. He denied him, so he said: I am

celaleyn:105-105.t: ﴿حَقِيقٌ﴾ worthy ﴿عَلَى أَنْ﴾ i.e. بِأَنْ ("of…") ﴿لَا أَقُولَ عَلَى اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْحَقَّ﴾ In one reading it is with doubled yāʾ, so حَقِيقٌ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is أَنْ and what follows it ﴿قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِبَيِّنَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعِيَ﴾ to Syria ﴿بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ He had enslaved them.

celaleyn:106-106.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Pharaoh to him ﴿إِنْ كُنْتَ جِئْتَ بِآيَةٍ﴾ for your claim ﴿فَأْتِ بِهَا إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ﴾ in it

celaleyn:107-107.t: ﴿فَأَلْقَى عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ ثُعْبَانٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ a huge serpent

celaleyn:108-108.t: ﴿وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُ﴾ he drew it out of the opening of his garment ﴿فَإِذَا هِيَ بَيْضَاءُ﴾ radiant ﴿لِلنَّاظِرِينَ﴾ unlike the brownness it had before

celaleyn:109-109.t: ﴿قَالَ الْمَلَأُ مِنْ قَوْمِ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّ هَذَا لَسَاحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ surpassing in the knowledge of sorcery. In al-Shuʿarāʾ it is from the words of Pharaoh himself, so it is as though they said it with him by way of consultation.

celaleyn:110-110.t: ﴿يُرِيدُ أَنْ يُخْرِجَكُمْ مِنْ أَرْضِكُمْ فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:111-111.t: ﴿قَالُوا أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ﴾ postpone the matter of the two of them ﴿وَأَرْسِلْ فِي الْمَدَائِنِ حَاشِرِينَ﴾ gatherers

celaleyn:112-112.t: ﴿يَأْتُوكَ بِكُلِّ سَاحِرٍ﴾ — in one reading [سَحَّارٍ] — ﴿عَلِيمٍ﴾ who surpasses Moses in the knowledge of sorcery. So they gathered them.

celaleyn:113-113.t: ﴿وَجَاءَ السَّحَرَةُ فِرْعَوْنَ قَالُوا أَإِنَّ﴾ with both hamzas fully pronounced (taḥqīq) and with the second softened (tashīl), and with an alif inserted between them in both ways; [إِنَّ] ﴿لَنَا لَأَجْرًا إِنْ كُنَّا نَحْنُ الْغَالِبِينَ﴾

celaleyn:114-114.t: ﴿قَالَ نَعَمْ وَإِنَّكُمْ لَمِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:115-115.t: ﴿قَالُوا يَا مُوسَى إِمَّا أَنْ تُلْقِيَ﴾ your staff ﴿وَإِمَّا أَنْ نَكُونَ نَحْنُ الْمُلْقِينَ﴾ what we have with us

celaleyn:116-116.t: ﴿قَالَ أَلْقُوا﴾ an imperative granting permission for their throwing to come first, as a means to making the truth manifest ﴿فَلَمَّا أَلْقَوْا﴾ their ropes and their staffs ﴿سَحَرُوا أَعْيُنَ النَّاسِ﴾ turned them away from the reality of what they perceived ﴿وَاسْتَرْهَبُوهُمْ﴾ frightened them, as they were made to imagine them as snakes moving swiftly ﴿وَجَاءُوا بِسِحْرٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾

celaleyn:117-117.t: ﴿وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى مُوسَى أَنْ أَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَإِذَا هِيَ تَلْقَفُ﴾ with one of the two tāʾs of the original omitted: swallows; [تَلْقَفُ] ﴿مَا يَأْفِكُونَ﴾ what they transform by their deception

celaleyn:118-118.t: ﴿فَوَقَعَ الْحَقُّ﴾ was established and became manifest ﴿وَبَطَلَ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ of sorcery

celaleyn:119-119.t: ﴿فَغُلِبُوا﴾ i.e. Pharaoh and his people ﴿هُنَالِكَ وَانْقَلَبُوا صَاغِرِينَ﴾ became abased

celaleyn:120-120.t: ﴿وَأُلْقِيَ السَّحَرَةُ سَاجِدِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:121-121.t: ﴿قَالُوا آمَنَّا بِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:122-122.t: ﴿رَبِّ مُوسَى وَهَارُونَ﴾ because they knew that what they had witnessed of the staff could not come about by sorcery

celaleyn:123-123.t: ﴿قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ أَآمَنْتُمْ﴾ with both hamzas fully pronounced (taḥqīq), and with the second changed into an alif [آمَنْتُمْ] ﴿بِهِ﴾ in Moses ﴿قَبْلَ أَنْ آذَنَ﴾ I ﴿لَكُمْ إِنَّ هَذَا﴾ which you have done ﴿لَمَكْرٌ مَكَرْتُمُوهُ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ لِتُخْرِجُوا مِنْهَا أَهْلَهَا فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ what will befall you from me

celaleyn:124-124.t: ﴿لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِنْ خِلَافٍ﴾ i.e. the right hand of each one and his left foot ﴿ثُمَّ لَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾

celaleyn:125-125.t: ﴿قَالُوا إِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا﴾ after our death, in whatever way it may be ﴿مُنْقَلِبُونَ﴾ returning in the Hereafter

celaleyn:126-126.t: ﴿وَمَا تَنْقِمُ﴾ do you resent ﴿مِنَّا إِلَّا أَنْ آمَنَّا بِآيَاتِ رَبِّنَا لَمَّا جَاءَتْنَا رَبَّنَا أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا﴾ when what he has threatened us with is carried out, lest we revert to being disbelievers ﴿وَتَوَفَّنَا مُسْلِمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:127-127.t: ﴿وَقَالَ الْمَلَأُ مِنْ قَوْمِ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ to him ﴿أَتَذَرُ﴾ will you leave ﴿مُوسَى وَقَوْمَهُ لِيُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ by calling to oppose you ﴿وَيَذَرَكَ وَآلِهَتَكَ﴾ He had made small idols for them which they worshipped, and he said: I am your lord and their lord; that is why he said: "I am your lord most high." ﴿قَالَ سَنُقَتِّلُ﴾ with the doubled (shadda) and the light form ﴿أَبْنَاءَهُمْ﴾ the newborn ﴿وَنَسْتَحْيِي﴾ keep alive ﴿نِسَاءَهُمْ﴾ as we did with them before ﴿وَإِنَّا فَوْقَهُمْ قَاهِرُونَ﴾ powerful. So they did that to them, and the Children of Israel complained.

celaleyn:128-128.t: ﴿قَالَ مُوسَى لِقَوْمِهِ اسْتَعِينُوا بِاللَّهِ وَاصْبِرُوا﴾ under their harm ﴿إِنَّ الْأَرْضَ لِلَّهِ يُورِثُهَا﴾ gives it ﴿مَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَالْعَاقِبَةُ﴾ the praiseworthy ﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ those who fear Allah

celaleyn:129-129.t: ﴿قَالُوا أُوذِينَا مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَأْتِيَنَا وَمِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جِئْتَنَا قَالَ عَسَى رَبُّكُمْ أَنْ يُهْلِكَ عَدُوَّكُمْ وَيَسْتَخْلِفَكُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنْظُرَ كَيْفَ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ in it

celaleyn:130-130.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَخَذْنَا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ بِالسِّنِينَ﴾ with drought ﴿وَنَقْصٍ مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ﴾ take admonition and so believe

celaleyn:131-131.t: ﴿فَإِذَا جَاءَتْهُمُ الْحَسَنَةُ﴾ fertility and wealth ﴿قَالُوا لَنَا هَذِهِ﴾ i.e. we deserve it — and they did not give thanks for it ﴿وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ﴾ barrenness and affliction ﴿يَطَّيَّرُوا﴾ they ascribe ill omen ﴿بِمُوسَى وَمَنْ مَعَهُ﴾ of the believers ﴿أَلَا إِنَّمَا طَائِرُهُمْ﴾ their ill omen ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ He brings it upon them ﴿وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that what befalls them is from Him

celaleyn:132-132.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا﴾ to Moses ﴿مَهْمَا تَأْتِنَا بِهِ مِنْ آيَةٍ لِتَسْحَرَنَا بِهَا فَمَا نَحْنُ لَكَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ So he invoked against them.

celaleyn:133-133.t: ﴿فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ الطُّوفَانَ﴾ which was water that entered their houses and reached the throats of those sitting, for seven days ﴿وَالْجَرَادَ﴾ which ate their crops and fruits likewise ﴿وَالْقُمَّلَ﴾ weevils, or it is a kind of tick, which went after what the locusts had left ﴿وَالضَّفَادِعَ﴾ which filled their houses and their food ﴿وَالدَّمَ﴾ in their waters ﴿آيَاتٍ مُفَصَّلَاتٍ﴾ made clear ﴿فَاسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾ toward believing in them ﴿وَكَانُوا قَوْمًا مُجْرِمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:134-134.t: ﴿وَلَمَّا وَقَعَ عَلَيْهِمُ الرِّجْزُ﴾ the punishment ﴿قَالُوا يَا مُوسَى ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ بِمَا عَهِدَ عِنْدَكَ﴾ of removing the punishment from us if we believe ﴿لَئِنْ﴾ a lām of oath ﴿كَشَفْتَ عَنَّا الرِّجْزَ لَنُؤْمِنَنَّ لَكَ وَلَنُرْسِلَنَّ مَعَكَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾

celaleyn:135-135.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا كَشَفْنَا﴾ by the supplication of Moses ﴿عَنْهُمُ الرِّجْزَ إِلَى أَجَلٍ هُمْ بَالِغُوهُ إِذَا هُمْ يَنْكُثُونَ﴾ break their covenant and persist in their disbelief

celaleyn:136-136.t: ﴿فَانْتَقَمْنَا مِنْهُمْ فَأَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ فِي الْيَمِّ﴾ the salt sea ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾ because ﴿كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا وَكَانُوا عَنْهَا غَافِلِينَ﴾ not reflecting on them

celaleyn:137-137.t: ﴿وَأَوْرَثْنَا الْقَوْمَ الَّذِينَ كَانُوا يُسْتَضْعَفُونَ﴾ through enslavement, and they are the Children of Israel ﴿مَشَارِقَ الْأَرْضِ وَمَغَارِبَهَا الَّتِي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا﴾ with water and trees; a naʿt (adjective) of الْأَرْض, and it is Syria ﴿وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ الْحُسْنَى﴾ which is His saying {وَنُرِيدُ أَنْ نَمُنَّ عَلَى الَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ} ﴿عَلَى بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ بِمَا صَبَرُوا﴾ under the harm of their enemy ﴿وَدَمَّرْنَا﴾ We destroyed ﴿مَا كَانَ يَصْنَعُ فِرْعَوْنُ وَقَوْمُهُ﴾ of building ﴿وَمَا كَانُوا يَعْرِشُونَ﴾ with kasra and with ḍamma on the rāʾ: what they raised up of buildings

celaleyn:138-138.t: ﴿وَجَاوَزْنَا﴾ We brought across ﴿بِبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ الْبَحْرَ فَأَتَوْا﴾ they passed ﴿عَلَى قَوْمٍ يَعْكُفُونَ﴾ with ḍamma and with kasra on the kāf ﴿عَلَى أَصْنَامٍ لَهُمْ﴾ persisting in worshipping them ﴿قَالُوا يَا مُوسَى اجْعَلْ لَنَا إِلَهًا﴾ an idol that we may worship ﴿كَمَا لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ قَالَ إِنَّكُمْ قَوْمٌ تَجْهَلُونَ﴾ since you have met Allah's blessing upon you with what you said

celaleyn:139-139.t: ﴿إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ مُتَبَّرٌ﴾ perishing ﴿مَا هُمْ فِيهِ وَبَاطِلٌ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:140-140.t: ﴿قَالَ أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَبْغِيكُمْ إِلَهًا﴾ an object of worship; its original form is أَبْغِي لَكُمْ ("seek for you") ﴿وَهُوَ فَضَّلَكُمْ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ in your time, by what He mentioned in His saying:

celaleyn:141-141.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ أَنْجَيْنَاكُمْ﴾ — in one reading [أَنْجَاكُمْ] — ﴿مِنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ﴾ imposing on you and making you taste ﴿سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ﴾ its severest, which is: ﴿يُقَتِّلُونَ أَبْنَاءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ﴾ keeping alive ﴿نِسَاءَكُمْ وَفِي ذَلِكُمْ﴾ saving and punishment ﴿بَلَاءٌ﴾ a bestowal of favour or a trial ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ﴾ Will you not then take admonition and desist from what you said?

celaleyn:142-142.t: ﴿وَوَعَدْنَا﴾ with an alif and without it ﴿مُوسَى ثَلَاثِينَ لَيْلَةً﴾ at whose end We would speak to him, on condition that he fast them; they were Dhū al-Qaʿda. He fasted them, and when they were complete he disliked the changed smell of his mouth, so he used the tooth-stick; so Allah commanded him to fast ten more, so that He would speak to him with the changed smell of his mouth, as the Exalted said: ﴿وَأَتْمَمْنَاهَا بِعَشْرٍ﴾ of Dhū al-Ḥijja ﴿فَتَمَّ مِيقَاتُ رَبِّهِ﴾ the time of His promise to speak to him ﴿أَرْبَعِينَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿لَيْلَةً﴾ a tamyīz (specification) ﴿وَقَالَ مُوسَى لِأَخِيهِ هَارُونَ﴾ when going to the mountain for the intimate discourse ﴿اخْلُفْنِي﴾ be my deputy ﴿فِي قَوْمِي وَأَصْلِحْ﴾ their affair ﴿وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ الْمُفْسِدِينَ﴾ by agreeing with them in acts of disobedience

celaleyn:143-143.t: ﴿وَلَمَّا جَاءَ مُوسَى لِمِيقَاتِنَا﴾ i.e. at the time in which We had promised him speech ﴿وَكَلَّمَهُ رَبُّهُ﴾ without intermediary, a speech that he heard from every direction ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ أَرِنِي﴾ Yourself ﴿انْظُرْ إِلَيْكَ قَالَ لَنْ تَرَانِي﴾ i.e. you are not able to see Me; expressing it this way rather than "I shall not be seen" indicates the possibility of seeing Him, Exalted is He ﴿وَلَكِنِ انْظُرْ إِلَى الْجَبَلِ﴾ which is stronger than you ﴿فَإِنِ اسْتَقَرَّ﴾ remains firm ﴿مَكَانَهُ فَسَوْفَ تَرَانِي﴾ i.e. you will remain firm for seeing Me; otherwise you have no capacity ﴿فَلَمَّا تَجَلَّى رَبُّهُ﴾ i.e. there appeared of His light the measure of half the fingertip of the little finger, as in a hadith that al-Ḥākim declared sound ﴿لِلْجَبَلِ جَعَلَهُ دَكًّا﴾ with the short and the long form, i.e. pounded flat, level with the ground ﴿وَخَرَّ مُوسَى صَعِقًا﴾ fainting from the terror of what he saw ﴿فَلَمَّا أَفَاقَ قَالَ سُبْحَانَكَ﴾ declaring You transcendent ﴿تُبْتُ إِلَيْكَ﴾ from asking for what I was not commanded ﴿وَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ in my time

celaleyn:144-144.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ the Exalted to him ﴿يَا مُوسَى إِنِّي اصْطَفَيْتُكَ﴾ have chosen you ﴿عَلَى النَّاسِ﴾ the people of your time ﴿بِرِسَالَاتِي﴾ with the plural and the singular ﴿وَبِكَلَامِي﴾ i.e. My speaking to you ﴿فَخُذْ مَا آتَيْتُكَ﴾ of favour ﴿وَكُنْ مِنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ﴾ for My blessings

celaleyn:145-145.t: ﴿وَكَتَبْنَا لَهُ فِي الْأَلْوَاحِ﴾ i.e. the tablets of the Torah; they were of the lote-tree of the Garden, or of chrysolite or emerald, seven or ten ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ that is needed in religion ﴿مَوْعِظَةً وَتَفْصِيلًا﴾ an explanation ﴿لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ a badal (substitute) from the preposition and its genitive noun before it ﴿فَخُذْهَا﴾ "We said" being implied (muqaddar) ﴿بِقُوَّةٍ﴾ with earnestness and effort ﴿وَأْمُرْ قَوْمَكَ يَأْخُذُوا بِأَحْسَنِهَا سَأُرِيكُمْ دَارَ الْفَاسِقِينَ﴾ Pharaoh and his followers, which is Egypt, so that you take a lesson from them

celaleyn:146-146.t: ﴿سَأَصْرِفُ عَنْ آيَاتِيَ﴾ the proofs of My power among created things and others ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَكَبَّرُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ﴾ by My forsaking them, so that they do not show arrogance in them [Translator's note: the text reads «فَلَا يَتَكَبَّرُونَ فِيهَا» ("so that they do not show arrogance in them"); the common reading of al-Jalalayn here is «فَلَا يَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِيهَا» ("so that they do not reflect on them").] ﴿وَإِنْ يَرَوْا كُلَّ آيَةٍ لَا يُؤْمِنُوا بِهَا وَإِنْ يَرَوْا سَبِيلَ﴾ the way of ﴿الرُّشْدِ﴾ the guidance that has come from Allah ﴿لَا يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلًا﴾ they do not travel it ﴿وَإِنْ يَرَوْا سَبِيلَ الْغَيِّ﴾ misguidance ﴿يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلًا ذَلِكَ﴾ turning away ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا وَكَانُوا عَنْهَا غَافِلِينَ﴾ the like of it has preceded

celaleyn:147-147.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا وَلِقَاءِ الْآخِرَةِ﴾ the resurrection and other things ﴿حَبِطَتْ﴾ have come to nothing ﴿أَعْمَالُهُمْ﴾ the good they did in this world, such as maintaining ties of kinship and giving charity, so there is no reward for them because its condition is lacking ﴿هَلْ﴾ they are not ﴿يُجْزَوْنَ إِلَّا﴾ the recompense of ﴿مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ of denial and acts of disobedience

celaleyn:148-148.t: ﴿وَاتَّخَذَ قَوْمُ مُوسَى مِنْ بَعْدِهِ﴾ i.e. after his going to the intimate discourse ﴿مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ﴾ which they had borrowed from Pharaoh's people on the pretext of a wedding, and it remained with them ﴿عِجْلًا﴾ which al-Sāmirī cast for them from it ﴿جَسَدًا﴾ a badal (substitute): flesh and blood ﴿لَهُ خُوَارٌ﴾ i.e. an audible sound; it was transformed so by placing in its mouth the dust he had taken from the hoof of Gabriel, for its effect is life in whatever it is placed in. The second mafʿūl (object) of اتَّخَذَ is omitted, i.e. "as a god" ﴿أَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّهُ لَا يُكَلِّمُهُمْ وَلَا يَهْدِيهِمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ so how can it be taken as a god? ﴿اتَّخَذُوهُ﴾ as a god ﴿وَكَانُوا ظَالِمِينَ﴾ by taking it

celaleyn:149-149.t: ﴿وَلَمَّا سُقِطَ فِي أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ i.e. they regretted worshipping it ﴿وَرَأَوْا﴾ knew ﴿أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ ضَلُّوا﴾ by it; that was after Moses returned ﴿قَالُوا لَئِنْ لَمْ يَرْحَمْنَا رَبُّنَا وَيَغْفِرْ لَنَا﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ in both ﴿لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:150-150.t: ﴿وَلَمَّا رَجَعَ مُوسَى إِلَى قَوْمِهِ غَضْبَانَ﴾ on their account ﴿أَسِفًا﴾ intensely grieved ﴿قَالَ﴾ to them ﴿بِئْسَمَا﴾ i.e. evil is a deputyship ﴿خَلَفْتُمُونِي﴾ -hā ("it") ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِي﴾ this deputyship of yours, since you associated partners ﴿أَعَجِلْتُمْ أَمْرَ رَبِّكُمْ وَأَلْقَى الْأَلْوَاحَ﴾ the tablets of the Torah, in anger for his Lord, and they broke ﴿وَأَخَذَ بِرَأْسِ أَخِيهِ﴾ i.e. by his hair with his right hand and his beard with his left ﴿يَجُرُّهُ إِلَيْهِ﴾ in anger ﴿قَالَ﴾ O ﴿ابْنَ أُمِّ﴾ with kasra on the mīm, and with fatḥa [أُمَّ]; he meant أُمِّي ("my mother"), and mentioning her is more apt to soften his heart ﴿إِنَّ الْقَوْمَ اسْتَضْعَفُونِي وَكَادُوا﴾ came near ﴿يَقْتُلُونَنِي فَلَا تُشْمِتْ﴾ make rejoice ﴿بِيَ الْأَعْدَاءَ﴾ by your humiliating me ﴿وَلَا تَجْعَلْنِي مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ by worshipping the calf, in being held to account

celaleyn:151-151.t: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي﴾ what I did to my brother ﴿وَلِأَخِي﴾ he included him in the supplication to please him and to ward off the enemies' rejoicing at him ﴿وَأَدْخِلْنَا فِي رَحْمَتِكَ وَأَنْتَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ﴾ The Exalted said:

celaleyn:152-152.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا الْعِجْلَ﴾ as a god ﴿سَيَنَالُهُمْ غَضَبٌ﴾ punishment ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَذِلَّةٌ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾ So they were punished by the command to kill themselves, and abasement was stamped upon them until the Day of Resurrection ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ as We recompensed them ﴿نَجْزِي الْمُفْتَرِينَ﴾ against Allah, by associating partners and otherwise

celaleyn:153-153.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ عَمِلُوا السَّيِّئَاتِ ثُمَّ تَابُوا﴾ turned back from them ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِهَا وَآمَنُوا﴾ in Allah ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ مِنْ بَعْدِهَا﴾ i.e. the repentance ﴿لَغَفُورٌ﴾ to them ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ toward them

celaleyn:154-154.t: ﴿وَلَمَّا سَكَتَ﴾ subsided ﴿عَنْ مُوسَى الْغَضَبُ أَخَذَ الْأَلْوَاحَ﴾ which he had thrown down ﴿وَفِي نُسْخَتِهَا﴾ i.e. what was copied in them, i.e. written ﴿هُدًى﴾ from misguidance ﴿وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِرَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُونَ﴾ fear; the lām was put on the mafʿūl (object) because it is placed first

celaleyn:155-155.t: ﴿وَاخْتَارَ مُوسَى قَوْمَهُ سَبْعِينَ﴾ i.e. from his people ﴿رَجُلًا﴾ of those who had not worshipped the calf, by command of the Exalted ﴿لِمِيقَاتِنَا﴾ i.e. for the time at which We had promised him their coming, so that they might apologise for their companions' worship of the calf; so he went out with them ﴿فَلَمَّا أَخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ﴾ the violent earthquake. Ibn ʿAbbās said: because they did not separate from their people when they worshipped the calf. He said: and they were other than those who asked for the vision and were seized by the thunderbolt ﴿قَالَ﴾ Moses ﴿رَبِّ لَوْ شِئْتَ أَهْلَكْتَهُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ i.e. before my going out with them, so that the Children of Israel would witness that and not suspect me ﴿وَإِيَّايَ أَتُهْلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ السُّفَهَاءُ مِنَّا﴾ a question seeking compassion, i.e. do not punish us for the sin of others ﴿إِنْ﴾ it is not ﴿هِيَ﴾ i.e. the trial into which the foolish fell ﴿إِلَّا فِتْنَتُكَ﴾ Your testing ﴿تُضِلُّ بِهَا مَنْ تَشَاءُ﴾ to send astray ﴿وَتَهْدِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ﴾ to guide ﴿أَنْتَ وَلِيُّنَا﴾ the One in charge of our affairs ﴿فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الْغَافِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:156-156.t: ﴿وَاكْتُبْ﴾ make due ﴿لَنَا فِي هَذِهِ الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ﴾ good ﴿إِنَّا هُدْنَا﴾ we have repented ﴿إِلَيْكَ قَالَ﴾ the Exalted ﴿عَذَابِي أُصِيبُ بِهِ مَنْ أَشَاءُ﴾ to punish ﴿وَرَحْمَتِي وَسِعَتْ﴾ encompasses ﴿كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾ in this world ﴿فَسَأَكْتُبُهَا﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَوةَ وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ بِآيَاتِنَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

celaleyn:157-157.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ الرَّسُولَ النَّبِيَّ الْأُمِّيَّ﴾ Muḥammad ﷺ ﴿الَّذِي يَجِدُونَهُ مَكْتُوبًا عِنْدَهُمْ فِي التَّوْرَاةِ وَالْإِنْجِيلِ﴾ by his name and his description ﴿يَأْمُرُهُمْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَاهُمْ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ الطَّيِّبَاتِ﴾ of what was forbidden in their law ﴿وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْخَبَائِثَ﴾ carrion and the like ﴿وَيَضَعُ عَنْهُمْ إِصْرَهُمْ﴾ their burden ﴿وَالْأَغْلَالَ﴾ the hardships ﴿الَّتِي كَانَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ such as killing oneself in repentance and cutting away the trace of impurity ﴿فَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِهِ﴾ among them ﴿وَعَزَّرُوهُ﴾ honoured him ﴿وَنَصَرُوهُ وَاتَّبَعُوا النُّورَ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ مَعَهُ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾

celaleyn:158-158.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an address to the Prophet ﷺ ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ جَمِيعًا الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ النَّبِيِّ الْأُمِّيِّ الَّذِي يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَكَلِمَاتِهِ﴾ the Quran ﴿وَاتَّبِعُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ﴾ be rightly guided

celaleyn:159-159.t: ﴿وَمِنْ قَوْمِ مُوسَى أُمَّةٌ﴾ a group ﴿يَهْدُونَ﴾ people ﴿بِالْحَقِّ وَبِهِ يَعْدِلُونَ﴾ in judgement

celaleyn:160-160.t: ﴿وَقَطَّعْنَاهُمْ﴾ We divided the Children of Israel ﴿اثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿أَسْبَاطًا﴾ a badal (substitute) from it, i.e. tribes ﴿أُمَمًا﴾ a badal from what precedes it ﴿وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى مُوسَى إِذِ اسْتَسْقَاهُ قَوْمُهُ﴾ in the wilderness ﴿أَنِ اضْرِبْ بِعَصَاكَ الْحَجَرَ﴾ and he struck it ﴿فَانْبَجَسَتْ﴾ gushed forth ﴿مِنْهُ اثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا﴾ by the number of the tribes ﴿قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ﴾ each tribe of them ﴿مَشْرَبَهُمْ وَظَلَّلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ الْغَمَامَ﴾ in the wilderness, from the heat of the sun ﴿وَأَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ الْمَنَّ وَالسَّلْوَى﴾ they are taranjabīn (manna) and quails (al-sumānī, with light mīm and short final vowel), and We said to them: ﴿كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَكِنْ كَانُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:161-161.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ قِيلَ لَهُمُ اسْكُنُوا هَذِهِ الْقَرْيَةَ﴾ Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) ﴿وَكُلُوا مِنْهَا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمْ وَقُولُوا﴾ our affair is ﴿حِطَّةٌ وَادْخُلُوا الْبَابَ﴾ i.e. the gate of the town ﴿سُجَّدًا﴾ a prostration of bowing ﴿نَغْفِرْ﴾ with nūn, and with tāʾ in the passive ﴿لَكُمْ خَطِيئَاتِكُمْ سَنَزِيدُ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ by obedience, in reward

celaleyn:162-162.t: ﴿فَبَدَّلَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْهُمْ قَوْلًا غَيْرَ الَّذِي قِيلَ لَهُمْ﴾ They said: "A grain in a hair", and entered shuffling on their backsides ﴿فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ رِجْزًا﴾ a punishment ﴿مِنَ السَّمَاءِ بِمَا كَانُوا يَظْلِمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:163-163.t: ﴿وَاسْأَلْهُمْ﴾ O Muḥammad, by way of rebuke ﴿عَنِ الْقَرْيَةِ الَّتِي كَانَتْ حَاضِرَةَ الْبَحْرِ﴾ adjacent to the Sea of al-Qulzum, and it is Ayla — what befell its people ﴿إِذْ يَعْدُونَ﴾ transgressed ﴿فِي السَّبْتِ﴾ by catching fish, which they had been commanded to leave on it ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) for يَعْدُونَ ﴿تَأْتِيهِمْ حِيتَانُهُمْ يَوْمَ سَبْتِهِمْ شُرَّعًا﴾ visible on the water ﴿وَيَوْمَ لَا يَسْبِتُونَ﴾ do not honour the Sabbath, i.e. the rest of the days ﴿لَا تَأْتِيهِمْ﴾ as a trial from Allah ﴿كَذَلِكَ نَبْلُوهُمْ بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ﴾ When they caught the fish, the town split into thirds: a third fished with them, a third forbade them, and a third refrained from both fishing and forbidding.

celaleyn:164-164.t: ﴿وَإِذْ﴾ conjoined to the إِذْ before it ﴿قَالَتْ أُمَّةٌ مِنْهُمْ﴾ which neither fished nor forbade, to those who forbade ﴿لِمَ تَعِظُونَ قَوْمًا اللَّهُ مُهْلِكُهُمْ أَوْ مُعَذِّبُهُمْ عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا قَالُوا﴾ our admonition is ﴿مَعْذِرَةٌ﴾ by which we excuse ourselves; [مَعْذِرَةً] ﴿إِلَى رَبِّكُمْ﴾ lest we be charged with negligence in abandoning forbidding ﴿وَلَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ﴾ the fishing

celaleyn:165-165.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا نَسُوا﴾ abandoned ﴿مَا ذُكِّرُوا﴾ were admonished ﴿بِهِ﴾ and did not turn back ﴿أَنْجَيْنَا الَّذِينَ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ السُّوءِ وَأَخَذْنَا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا﴾ by transgressing ﴿بِعَذَابٍ بَئِيسٍ﴾ severe ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ﴾

celaleyn:166-166.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا عَتَوْا﴾ were too proud ﴿عَنْ﴾ to abandon ﴿مَا نُهُوا عَنْهُ قُلْنَا لَهُمْ كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ﴾ abased — and they became so. This is a detailing of what preceded it. Ibn ʿAbbās said: I do not know what was done with the silent party. ʿIkrima said: It did not perish, because it disliked what they did and said "Why do you admonish…" etc. And al-Ḥākim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he came round to it and it pleased him.

celaleyn:167-167.t: ﴿وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ﴾ made known ﴿رَبُّكَ لَيَبْعَثَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ i.e. the Jews ﴿إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَمَةِ مَنْ يَسُومُهُمْ سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ﴾ through abasement and the taking of jizya (poll-tax). So He sent Solomon against them, and after him Nebuchadnezzar, who killed them, took them captive and imposed jizya on them; they paid it to the Magians until our Prophet ﷺ was sent, and he imposed it on them ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَسَرِيعُ الْعِقَابِ﴾ for whoever disobeys Him ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَغَفُورٌ﴾ to the people of obedience to Him ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ toward them

celaleyn:168-168.t: ﴿وَقَطَّعْنَاهُمْ﴾ We dispersed them ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ أُمَمًا﴾ groups ﴿مِنْهُمُ الصَّالِحُونَ وَمِنْهُمْ﴾ people ﴿دُونَ ذَلِكَ﴾ the disbelievers and the transgressors ﴿وَبَلَوْنَاهُمْ بِالْحَسَنَاتِ﴾ with blessings ﴿وَالسَّيِّئَاتِ﴾ afflictions ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ from their transgression

celaleyn:169-169.t: ﴿فَخَلَفَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ خَلْفٌ وَرِثُوا الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Torah, from their fathers ﴿يَأْخُذُونَ عَرَضَ هَذَا الْأَدْنَى﴾ i.e. the debris of this lowly thing, i.e. this world, lawful and unlawful ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ سَيُغْفَرُ لَنَا﴾ what we have done ﴿وَإِنْ يَأْتِهِمْ عَرَضٌ مِثْلُهُ يَأْخُذُوهُ﴾ The clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. they hope for forgiveness while returning to what they did, persisting in it; and there is no promise of forgiveness with persistence in the Torah ﴿أَلَمْ يُؤْخَذْ﴾ a question of affirmation (istifhām taqrīr) ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ مِيثَاقُ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the annexation (iḍāfa) is in the sense of فِي ("in") ﴿أَنْ لَا يَقُولُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْحَقَّ وَدَرَسُوا﴾ conjoined to يُؤْخَذْ: they read ﴿مَا فِيهِ﴾ so why did they lie against Him by ascribing forgiveness with persistence to Him? ﴿وَالدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ﴾ the unlawful ﴿أَفَلَا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ [تَعْقِلُونَ], that it is better, and so prefer it to this world

celaleyn:170-170.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يُمَسِّكُونَ﴾ with the doubled (shadda) and the light form ﴿بِالْكِتَابِ﴾ among them ﴿وَأَقَامُوا الصَّلَوةَ﴾ such as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his companions ﴿إِنَّا لَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُصْلِحِينَ﴾ The clause is the khabar (predicate) of الَّذِينَ, and in it the overt noun is put in place of the pronoun, i.e. "their reward".

celaleyn:171-171.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ نَتَقْنَا الْجَبَلَ﴾ We raised it from its base ﴿فَوْقَهُمْ كَأَنَّهُ ظُلَّةٌ وَظَنُّوا﴾ were certain ﴿أَنَّهُ وَاقِعٌ بِهِمْ﴾ falling upon them, by Allah's promising them that it would fall if they did not accept the rulings of the Torah; they had refused them because of their heaviness, so they accepted. And We said to them: ﴿خُذُوا مَا آتَيْنَاكُمْ بِقُوَّةٍ﴾ with earnestness and effort ﴿وَاذْكُرُوا مَا فِيهِ﴾ by acting on it ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ﴾

celaleyn:172-172.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ﴾ when ﴿أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ﴾ a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from what precedes it, with the preposition repeated ﴿ذُرِّيَّاتِهِمْ﴾ [ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ] by bringing some of them out of the loins of others, from the loins of Adam, generation after generation, in the way they are born, like tiny ants, at Nuʿmān on the day of ʿArafa; and He set up for them proofs of His lordship and placed reason in them ﴿وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ He said: ﴿أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا بَلَى﴾ You are our Lord ﴿شَهِدْنَا﴾ to that. And the making them bear witness is so ﴿أَنْ﴾ not ﴿يَقُولُوا﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ [تَقُولُوا] in both places, i.e. the disbelievers ﴿يَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنْ هَذَا﴾ affirmation of oneness (tawḥīd) ﴿غَافِلِينَ﴾ not knowing it

celaleyn:173-173.t: ﴿أَوْ يَقُولُوا إِنَّمَا أَشْرَكَ آبَاؤُنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ i.e. before us; [تَقُولُوا] ﴿وَكُنَّا ذُرِّيَّةً مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ﴾ so we followed them ﴿أَفَتُهْلِكُنَا﴾ will You punish us ﴿بِمَا فَعَلَ الْمُبْطِلُونَ﴾ among our fathers, by founding the association of partners. The meaning: they cannot argue with that, given that they were made to bear witness against themselves to tawḥīd, and reminding of it on the tongue of the possessor of the miracle stands in place of its being remembered in the souls.

celaleyn:174-174.t: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ الْآيَاتِ﴾ We make them clear, as We made clear the covenant, so that they reflect on them ﴿وَلَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ from their disbelief

celaleyn:175-175.t: ﴿وَاتْلُ﴾ O Muḥammad ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ i.e. the Jews ﴿نَبَأَ﴾ the report of ﴿الَّذِي آتَيْنَاهُ آيَاتِنَا فَانْسَلَخَ مِنْهَا﴾ went out of them by his disbelief as a snake goes out of its skin. He was Balʿam ibn Bāʿūrāʾ, one of the scholars of the Children of Israel; he was asked to invoke against Moses and something was given to him as a gift, so he invoked, and it turned back on him and his tongue lolled out onto his chest ﴿فَأَتْبَعَهُ الشَّيْطَانُ﴾ caught up with him and became his companion ﴿فَكَانَ مِنَ الْغَاوِينَ﴾

celaleyn:176-176.t: ﴿وَلَوْ شِئْنَا لَرَفَعْنَاهُ﴾ to the ranks of the scholars ﴿بِهَا﴾ by enabling him to act ﴿وَلَكِنَّهُ أَخْلَدَ﴾ settled ﴿إِلَى الْأَرْضِ﴾ i.e. this world, and inclined to it ﴿وَاتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ﴾ in his invoking toward it, so We lowered him ﴿فَمَثَلُهُ﴾ his description ﴿كَمَثَلِ الْكَلْبِ إِنْ تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْهِ﴾ by driving away and chiding ﴿يَلْهَثْ﴾ lolls out its tongue ﴿أَوْ﴾ if ﴿تَتْرُكْهُ يَلْهَثْ﴾ and no other animal is like that. The two conditional clauses are a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. panting and abased in every state. The intent is the likening in lowliness and baseness, as indicated by the fāʾ that signals that what follows it results from what precedes it — inclining to this world and following desire — and as indicated by His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ مَثَلُ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا فَاقْصُصِ الْقَصَصَ﴾ to the Jews ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ﴾ reflect on them and so believe

celaleyn:177-177.t: ﴿سَاءَ﴾ evil is ﴿مَثَلًا الْقَوْمُ﴾ i.e. the likeness of the people ﴿الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا وَأَنْفُسَهُمْ كَانُوا يَظْلِمُونَ﴾ by denial

celaleyn:178-178.t: ﴿مَنْ يَهْدِ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ الْمُهْتَدِي وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:179-179.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ ذَرَأْنَا﴾ We have created ﴿لِجَهَنَّمَ كَثِيرًا مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ لَهُمْ قُلُوبٌ لَا يَفْقَهُونَ بِهَا﴾ the truth ﴿وَلَهُمْ أَعْيُنٌ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ بِهَا﴾ the proofs of Allah's power, with a seeing that takes a lesson ﴿وَلَهُمْ آذَانٌ لَا يَسْمَعُونَ بِهَا﴾ the signs and admonitions, with a hearing of reflection and taking admonition ﴿أُولَئِكَ كَالْأَنْعَامِ﴾ in lacking understanding, sight and hearing ﴿بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ﴾ than cattle, because they seek their benefits and flee their harms, whereas these advance upon the Fire in obstinacy ﴿أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْغَافِلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:180-180.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى﴾ the ninety-nine mentioned in the hadith; الْحُسْنَى is the feminine of الْأَحْسَن ﴿فَادْعُوهُ﴾ name Him ﴿بِهَا وَذَرُوا﴾ leave ﴿الَّذِينَ يُلْحِدُونَ﴾ from أَلْحَدَ and لَحَدَ: they deviate from the truth ﴿فِي أَسْمَائِهِ﴾ in that they derived from them names for their gods, such as al-Lāt from Allāh, al-ʿUzzā from al-ʿAzīz and Manāt from al-Mannān ﴿سَيُجْزَوْنَ﴾ in the Hereafter [Translator's note: the text has مِنَ الْآخِرَةِ ("from the Hereafter")], the recompense of ﴿مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ This was before the command to fight.

celaleyn:181-181.t: ﴿وَمِمَّنْ خَلَقْنَا أُمَّةٌ يَهْدُونَ بِالْحَقِّ وَبِهِ يَعْدِلُونَ﴾ They are the community of Muḥammad ﷺ, as in a hadith.

celaleyn:182-182.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ the Quran, of the people of Mecca ﴿سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ﴾ We shall take them little by little ﴿مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:183-183.t: ﴿وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ﴾ I give them respite ﴿إِنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ﴾ severe, unbearable

celaleyn:184-184.t: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَتَفَكَّرُوا﴾ and so know ﴿مَا بِصَاحِبِهِمْ﴾ Muḥammad ﷺ ﴿مِنْ جِنَّةٍ﴾ madness ﴿إِنْ﴾ he is not ﴿هُوَ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ clear in warning

celaleyn:185-185.t: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَنْظُرُوا فِي مَلَكُوتِ﴾ the dominion of ﴿السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَ﴾ in ﴿مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾ an explication (bayān) of مَا — and so infer from it the power of its Maker and His oneness ﴿وَ﴾ in ﴿أَنْ﴾ i.e. أَنَّهُ ("that…") ﴿عَسَى أَنْ يَكُونَ قَدِ اقْتَرَبَ﴾ has drawn near ﴿أَجَلُهُمْ﴾ so that they die disbelievers and go to the Fire — and so hasten to faith ﴿فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَهُ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

celaleyn:186-186.t: ﴿مَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَلَا هَادِيَ لَهُ وَيَذَرُهُمْ﴾ with yāʾ and with nūn, with the nominative as a resumption (istiʾnāf), and with the jussive conjoined to the position of what follows the fāʾ ﴿فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ﴾ wandering to and fro in bewilderment

celaleyn:187-187.t: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ﴾ i.e. the people of Mecca ﴿عَنِ السَّاعَةِ﴾ the Resurrection ﴿أَيَّانَ﴾ when ﴿مُرْسَاهَا قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿إِنَّمَا عِلْمُهَا﴾ of when it will be ﴿عِنْدَ رَبِّي لَا يُجَلِّيهَا﴾ manifests it ﴿لِوَقْتِهَا﴾ the lām is in the sense of فِي ("at") ﴿إِلَّا هُوَ ثَقُلَتْ﴾ it weighs heavily ﴿فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ upon their inhabitants, because of its terror ﴿لَا تَأْتِيكُمْ إِلَّا بَغْتَةً﴾ suddenly ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ كَأَنَّكَ حَفِيٌّ﴾ persistent in asking ﴿عَنْهَا﴾ until you came to know it ﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَا عِلْمُهَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ an emphasis ﴿وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that its knowledge is with Him, Exalted is He

celaleyn:188-188.t: ﴿قُلْ لَا أَمْلِكُ لِنَفْسِي نَفْعًا﴾ to bring it ﴿وَلَا ضَرًّا﴾ to ward it off ﴿إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ وَلَوْ كُنْتُ أَعْلَمُ الْغَيْبَ﴾ what is hidden from me ﴿لَاسْتَكْثَرْتُ مِنَ الْخَيْرِ وَمَا مَسَّنِيَ السُّوءُ﴾ of poverty and other things, because I would guard against it by avoiding harms ﴿إِنْ﴾ I am not ﴿أَنَا إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ﴾ of the Fire to the disbelievers ﴿وَبَشِيرٌ﴾ of the Garden ﴿لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

celaleyn:189-189.t: ﴿هُوَ﴾ i.e. Allah ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ﴾ i.e. Adam ﴿وَجَعَلَ﴾ created ﴿مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا﴾ Eve ﴿لِيَسْكُنَ إِلَيْهَا﴾ and be at ease with her ﴿فَلَمَّا تَغَشَّاهَا﴾ had intercourse with her ﴿حَمَلَتْ حَمْلًا خَفِيفًا﴾ which is the sperm-drop ﴿فَمَرَّتْ بِهِ﴾ she went about and came, because of its lightness ﴿فَلَمَّا أَثْقَلَتْ﴾ with the growth of the child in her womb, and they both feared it might be a beast ﴿دَعَوَا اللَّهَ رَبَّهُمَا لَئِنْ آتَيْتَنَا﴾ a child ﴿صَالِحًا﴾ sound ﴿لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ﴾ to You for it

celaleyn:190-190.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا آتَاهُمَا﴾ a child ﴿صَالِحًا جَعَلَا لَهُ شُرَكَاءَ﴾ — in one reading with kasra on the shīn and tanwīn, i.e. a partner — ﴿فِيمَا آتَاهُمَا﴾ by naming him ʿAbd al-Ḥārith ("servant of al-Ḥārith"), whereas one should be a servant only of Allah; it is not association in worship, because of Adam's protection from sin. Samura narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "When Eve gave birth, Iblīs went around her — no child of hers used to survive — and said: Name him ʿAbd al-Ḥārith and he will live. So she named him and he lived; and that was from the suggestion of Satan and his command." Al-Ḥākim narrated it and said it is sound (ṣaḥīḥ), and al-Tirmidhī, who said it is ḥasan gharīb ﴿فَتَعَالَى اللَّهُ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ i.e. the people of Mecca, associating idols with Him. The clause is a consequence, conjoined to خَلَقَكُمْ, and what is between them is a parenthetical insertion.

celaleyn:191-191.t: ﴿أَيُشْرِكُونَ﴾ with Him in worship ﴿مَا لَا يَخْلُقُ شَيْئًا وَهُمْ يُخْلَقُونَ﴾

celaleyn:192-192.t: ﴿وَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ لَهُمْ﴾ i.e. for their worshippers ﴿نَصْرًا وَلَا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَنْصُرُونَ﴾ by protecting them from whoever intends them harm, by breaking or otherwise. The question is for rebuke.

celaleyn:193-193.t: ﴿وَإِنْ تَدْعُوهُمْ﴾ i.e. the idols ﴿إِلَى الْهُدَى لَا يَتَّبِعُوكُمْ﴾ with the light and the doubled (shadda) form ﴿سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ أَدَعَوْتُمُوهُمْ﴾ to it ﴿أَمْ أَنْتُمْ صَامِتُونَ﴾ from calling them — they do not follow it, because they do not hear

celaleyn:194-194.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ﴾ worship ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ عِبَادٌ﴾ owned ﴿أَمْثَالُكُمْ فَادْعُوهُمْ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لَكُمْ﴾ your call ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ in that they are gods. Then He made clear the extremity of their incapacity and the superiority of their worshippers over them, and said:

celaleyn:195-195.t: ﴿أَلَهُمْ أَرْجُلٌ يَمْشُونَ بِهَا أَمْ﴾ rather, do ﴿لَهُمْ أَيْدٍ﴾ plural of يَد ﴿يَبْطِشُونَ بِهَا أَمْ﴾ rather, do ﴿لَهُمْ أَعْيُنٌ يُبْصِرُونَ بِهَا أَمْ﴾ rather, do ﴿لَهُمْ آذَانٌ يَسْمَعُونَ بِهَا﴾ a question of disavowal (istifhām inkārī), i.e. they have none of that which you have, so how can you worship them when you are more complete in state than they? ﴿قُلِ﴾ to them, O Muḥammad ﴿ادْعُوا شُرَكَاءَكُمْ﴾ to my destruction ﴿ثُمَّ كِيدُونِ فَلَا تُنْظِرُونِ﴾ give respite, for I do not care about you

celaleyn:196-196.t: ﴿إِنَّ وَلِيِّيَ اللَّهُ﴾ the One in charge of my affairs ﴿الَّذِي نَزَّلَ الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Quran ﴿وَهُوَ يَتَوَلَّى الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ by His protection

celaleyn:197-197.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَكُمْ وَلَا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَنْصُرُونَ﴾ so how should I care about them?

celaleyn:198-198.t: ﴿وَإِنْ تَدْعُوهُمْ﴾ i.e. the idols ﴿إِلَى الْهُدَى لَا يَسْمَعُوا وَتَرَاهُمْ﴾ i.e. the idols, O Muḥammad ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَيْكَ﴾ i.e. they face you like one looking ﴿وَهُمْ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:199-199.t: ﴿خُذِ الْعَفْوَ﴾ what is easy of people's characters, and do not probe into them ﴿وَأْمُرْ بِالْعُرْفِ﴾ the right ﴿وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ الْجَاهِلِينَ﴾ and do not meet them with their foolishness

celaleyn:200-200.t: ﴿وَإِمَّا﴾ in it the nūn of the conditional إِنْ is assimilated (idghām) into the redundant (zāʾida) مَا ﴿يَنْزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ نَزْغٌ﴾ i.e. if something diverts you from what you have been commanded ﴿فَاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ﴾ the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the response to the imperative is omitted, i.e. "He will ward it off from you" ﴿إِنَّهُ سَمِيعٌ﴾ of speech ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of action

celaleyn:201-201.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا إِذَا مَسَّهُمْ﴾ befalls them ﴿طَيْفٌ﴾ — in one reading [طَائِفٌ] — i.e. something that comes upon them ﴿مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ تَذَكَّرُوا﴾ Allah's punishment and His reward ﴿فَإِذَا هُمْ مُبْصِرُونَ﴾ the truth from what is other than it, and so they turn back

celaleyn:202-202.t: ﴿وَإِخْوَانُهُمْ﴾ i.e. the brothers of the devils, among the disbelievers ﴿يَمُدُّونَهُمْ﴾ i.e. the devils ﴿فِي الْغَيِّ ثُمَّ﴾ they ﴿لَا يُقْصِرُونَ﴾ desist from it by gaining insight, as the God-fearing gained insight

celaleyn:203-203.t: ﴿وَإِذَا لَمْ تَأْتِهِمْ﴾ i.e. the people of Mecca ﴿بِآيَةٍ﴾ of those they proposed ﴿قَالُوا لَوْلَا﴾ why not ﴿اجْتَبَيْتَهَا﴾ produced it of your own accord ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿إِنَّمَا أَتَّبِعُ مَا يُوحَى إِلَيَّ مِنْ رَبِّي﴾ and it is not for me to bring anything of my own accord ﴿هَذَا﴾ Quran ﴿بَصَائِرُ﴾ proofs ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةٌ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

celaleyn:204-204.t: ﴿وَإِذَا قُرِئَ الْقُرْآنُ فَاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ وَأَنْصِتُوا﴾ from speaking ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ﴾ It was revealed concerning refraining from speech during the sermon (khuṭba); it is expressed as "the Quran" because it contains it. It is also said: concerning the recitation of the Quran in general.

celaleyn:205-205.t: ﴿وَاذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ فِي نَفْسِكَ﴾ i.e. secretly ﴿تَضَرُّعًا﴾ in humility ﴿وَخِيفَةً﴾ fear of Him ﴿وَ﴾ above secrecy ﴿دُونَ الْجَهْرِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ﴾ i.e. moderately, between the two ﴿بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْآصَالِ﴾ the beginnings of the day and its ends ﴿وَلَا تَكُنْ مِنَ الْغَافِلِينَ﴾ of the remembrance of Allah

celaleyn:206-206.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ﴾ i.e. the angels ﴿لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ are not too proud ﴿عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِ وَيُسَبِّحُونَهُ﴾ declare Him transcendent above what does not befit Him ﴿وَلَهُ يَسْجُدُونَ﴾ i.e. they single Him out for submission and worship; so be like them.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿المص﴾ Allah knows best what He means by it. This is

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿كِتَابٌ أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ﴾ an address to the Prophet ﷺ; ﴿فَلَا يَكُنْ فِي صَدْرِكَ حَرَجٌ﴾ tightness ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ about conveying it, for fear of being denied; ﴿لِتُنْذِرَ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) أُنْزِلَ, i.e. for warning with it, ﴿وَذِكْرَى﴾ a reminder ﴿لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ in it. Say to them:

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿اتَّبِعُوا مَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ i.e. the Qur'an, ﴿وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا﴾ take ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ i.e. Allah, i.e. other than Him, ﴿أَوْلِيَاءَ﴾ whom you obey in disobeying Him, the Exalted. ﴿قَلِيلًا مَا تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ with tāʾ and with yāʾ [يَذَّكَّرُونَ]: take admonition; in it the originally present tāʾ is assimilated (idghām) into the dhāl, and in one reading it is with sukūn on it [تَذْكُرُونَ]. And مَا is redundant (zāʾida), to emphasize the fewness.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَكَمْ﴾ predicative (khabariyya), an object (mafʿūl), ﴿مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ﴾ its people are meant, ﴿أَهْلَكْنَاهَا﴾ We willed to destroy it, ﴿فَجَاءَهَا بَأْسُنَا﴾ Our punishment ﴿بَيَاتًا﴾ by night ﴿أَوْ هُمْ قَائِلُونَ﴾ sleeping at midday. Al-qaylūla is resting at midday, even if there is no sleep with it. I.e. at one time it came to it by night and at another time by day.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿فَمَا كَانَ دَعْوَاهُمْ﴾ their saying ﴿إِذْ جَاءَهُمْ بَأْسُنَا إِلَّا أَنْ قَالُوا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿فَلَنَسْأَلَنَّ الَّذِينَ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ i.e. the nations, about their response to the messengers and their deeds regarding what was conveyed to them, ﴿وَلَنَسْأَلَنَّ الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾ about the conveying.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿فَلَنَقُصَّنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ بِعِلْمٍ﴾ We will inform them, from knowledge, of what they did, ﴿وَمَا كُنَّا غَائِبِينَ﴾ from the messengers' conveying, nor from the past nations in what they did.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَالْوَزْنُ﴾ of deeds, or of their records, with a balance that has a tongue and two pans, as has come in the hadith, takes place ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ i.e. on the day of the aforementioned questioning, which is the Day of Resurrection; ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾ the just — an adjective (ṣifa) of الْوَزْنُ. ﴿فَمَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ﴾ with good deeds, ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾ the successful.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَمَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ﴾ with bad deeds, ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ by consigning them to the Fire, ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا بِآيَاتِنَا يَظْلِمُونَ﴾ deny.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ مَكَّنَّاكُمْ﴾ O children of Ādam, ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ وَجَعَلْنَا لَكُمْ فِيهَا مَعَايِشَ﴾ with yāʾ: means by which you live, the plural of مَعِيشَة. ﴿قَلِيلًا مَا﴾ to emphasize the fewness ﴿تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ for that.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَاكُمْ﴾ i.e. your father Ādam, ﴿ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَاكُمْ﴾ i.e. We formed him while you were in his loins; ﴿ثُمَّ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ﴾ a prostration of greeting, by bowing, ﴿فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ﴾ the father of the jinn, who was among the angels; ﴿لَمْ يَكُنْ مِنَ السَّاجِدِينَ﴾

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ the Exalted: ﴿مَا مَنَعَكَ أَنْ لَا﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿تَسْجُدَ إِذْ﴾ when ﴿أَمَرْتُكَ قَالَ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِي مِنْ نَارٍ وَخَلَقْتَهُ مِنْ طِينٍ﴾

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿قَالَ فَاهْبِطْ مِنْهَا﴾ i.e. from Paradise — and it is said: from the heavens — ﴿فَمَا يَكُونُ﴾ it is not fitting ﴿لَكَ أَنْ تَتَكَبَّرَ فِيهَا فَاخْرُجْ﴾ from it; ﴿إِنَّكَ مِنَ الصَّاغِرِينَ﴾ the abased.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿قَالَ أَنْظِرْنِي﴾ give me respite ﴿إِلَى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾ i.e. people.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿قَالَ إِنَّكَ مِنَ الْمُنْظَرِينَ﴾ and in another ayah: {إِلَى يَوْمِ الْوَقْتِ الْمَعْلُومِ}, i.e. the day of the first blowing [of the Trumpet].

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿قَالَ فَبِمَا أَغْوَيْتَنِي﴾ i.e. by Your leading me astray — the bāʾ is for oath (qasam), and its answer (jawāb) is — ﴿لَأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ﴾ i.e. for the children of Ādam ﴿صِرَاطَكَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ﴾ i.e. on the path that leads to You.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿ثُمَّ لَآتِيَنَّهُمْ مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ وَعَنْ أَيْمَانِهِمْ وَعَنْ شَمَائِلِهِمْ﴾ i.e. from every direction, and prevent them from travelling it. Ibn ʿAbbās said: He cannot come from above them, lest he come between the servant and the mercy of Allah, the Exalted. ﴿وَلَا تَجِدُ أَكْثَرَهُمْ شَاكِرِينَ﴾ believers.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿قَالَ اخْرُجْ مِنْهَا مَذْءُومًا﴾ with hamza: disgraced, or detested, ﴿مَدْحُورًا﴾ banished from mercy. ﴿لَمَنْ تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ﴾ of people — the lām is the lām of commencement (ibtidāʾ), or one that prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam), and that [oath] is: ﴿لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنْكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾ i.e. of you together with your offspring, and of people; in it the one present is given precedence over the one absent (taghlīb). And in the sentence there is the meaning of the apodosis (jazāʾ) of the conditional مَنْ, i.e. whoever follows you, I will punish him.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَ﴾ He said: ﴿يَا آدَمُ اسْكُنْ أَنْتَ﴾ a tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun in اسْكُنْ, so that something may be conjoined to it, ﴿وَزَوْجُكَ﴾ Ḥawwāʾ, with madd, ﴿الْجَنَّةَ فَكُلَا مِنْ حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَذِهِ الشَّجَرَةَ﴾ by eating from it — and it is wheat — ﴿فَتَكُونَا مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا الشَّيْطَانُ﴾ Iblīs, ﴿لِيُبْدِيَ﴾ to reveal ﴿لَهُمَا مَا وُورِيَ﴾ of the pattern fūʿila, from al-muwārāh (concealing), ﴿عَنْهُمَا مِنْ سَوْآتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَاكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَذِهِ الشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّا﴾ out of dislike ﴿أَنْ تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ﴾ — and it has been read with kasra on the lām [مَلِكَيْنِ] — ﴿أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ الْخَالِدِينَ﴾ i.e. and that follows necessarily from eating from it, as in another ayah: {هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَى شَجَرَةِ الْخُلْدِ وَمُلْكٍ لَا يَبْلَى}.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَقَاسَمَهُمَا﴾ i.e. he swore to them by Allah: ﴿إِنِّي لَكُمَا لَمِنَ النَّاصِحِينَ﴾ in that.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿فَدَلَّاهُمَا﴾ he brought them down from their rank ﴿بِغُرُورٍ﴾ on his part. ﴿فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا الشَّجَرَةَ﴾ i.e. ate from it, ﴿بَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْآتُهُمَا﴾ i.e. there appeared to each of them his own front private part and that of the other, and his rear; each of them is called a sawʾa because its exposure grieves (yasūʾu) its owner. ﴿وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ﴾ they began to stick ﴿عَلَيْهِمَا مِنْ وَرَقِ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ to cover themselves with it. ﴿وَنَادَاهُمَا رَبُّهُمَا أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُمَا عَنْ تِلْكُمَا الشَّجَرَةِ وَأَقُلْ لَكُمَا إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ لَكُمَا عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ﴾ clear in enmity; the interrogative is for eliciting acknowledgement (taqrīr).

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿قَالَا رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَا أَنْفُسَنَا﴾ by our disobedience, ﴿وَإِنْ لَمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿قَالَ اهْبِطُوا﴾ i.e. Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ, together with the offspring you contain; ﴿بَعْضُكُمْ﴾ some of the offspring ﴿لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ﴾ through some of them wronging others; ﴿وَلَكُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ﴾ i.e. a place of settling, ﴿وَمَتَاعٌ﴾ enjoyment ﴿إِلَى حِينٍ﴾ in which your terms come to an end.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿قَالَ فِيهَا﴾ i.e. the earth ﴿تَحْيَوْنَ وَفِيهَا تَمُوتُونَ وَمِنْهَا تُخْرَجُونَ﴾ by the resurrection — in the active and the passive [تَخْرُجُونَ].

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿يَا بَنِي آدَمَ قَدْ أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ لِبَاسًا﴾ i.e. We created it for you, ﴿يُوَارِي﴾ covering ﴿سَوْآتِكُمْ وَرِيشًا﴾ that is, clothing with which one adorns oneself; ﴿وَلِبَاسَ التَّقْوَى﴾ righteous deeds and good bearing — in the accusative, conjoined to لِبَاسًا, and in the nominative [وَلِبَاسُ] as a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the clause ﴿ذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ ذَلِكَ مِنْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ the proofs of His power, ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ﴾ and so believe — in it there is a shift (iltifāt) from the second person.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿يَا بَنِي آدَمَ لَا يَفْتِنَنَّكُمْ﴾ lead you astray ﴿الشَّيْطَانُ﴾ i.e. do not follow him and so be tempted, ﴿كَمَا أَخْرَجَ أَبَوَيْكُمْ﴾ by his temptation ﴿مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ يَنْزِعُ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿عَنْهُمَا لِبَاسَهُمَا لِيُرِيَهُمَا سَوْآتِهِمَا إِنَّهُ﴾ i.e. Satan ﴿يَرَاكُمْ هُوَ وَقَبِيلُهُ﴾ his troops ﴿مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا تَرَوْنَهُمْ﴾ because of the subtlety of their bodies, or their having no colours. ﴿إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا الشَّيَاطِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ﴾ helpers and companions ﴿لِلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿وَإِذَا فَعَلُوا فَاحِشَةً﴾ such as associating partners (shirk), and their circumambulating the House naked, saying, "We will not circumambulate in clothes in which we have disobeyed Allah," and they were forbidden it, ﴿قَالُوا وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهَا آبَاءَنَا﴾ and we followed them, ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَمَرَنَا بِهَا﴾ too. ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَأْمُرُ بِالْفَحْشَاءِ أَتَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that He said? — an interrogative of disapproval (inkār).

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿قُلْ أَمَرَ رَبِّي بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ justice, ﴿وَأَقِيمُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the meaning of بِالْقِسْطِ, i.e. He said: "Be just, and set," or before it "so turn [to Him]" is implied, ﴿وُجُوهَكُمْ﴾ to Allah ﴿عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ﴾ i.e. make your prostration sincerely for Him, ﴿وَادْعُوهُ﴾ worship Him, ﴿مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ﴾ free of associating partners. ﴿كَمَا بَدَأَكُمْ﴾ created you when you were nothing, ﴿تَعُودُونَ﴾ i.e. He will bring you back alive on the Day of Resurrection.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿فَرِيقًا﴾ of you ﴿هَدَى وَفَرِيقًا حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الضَّلَالَةُ إِنَّهُمُ اتَّخَذُوا الشَّيَاطِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him, ﴿وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ مُهْتَدُونَ﴾

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿يَا بَنِي آدَمَ خُذُوا زِينَتَكُمْ﴾ what covers your nakedness ﴿عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ﴾ at prayer and circumambulation; ﴿وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا﴾ what you wish, ﴿وَلَا تُسْرِفُوا إِنَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ in disapproval of them: ﴿مَنْ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي أَخْرَجَ لِعِبَادِهِ﴾ of clothing, ﴿وَالطَّيِّبَاتِ﴾ the delightful things ﴿مِنَ الرِّزْقِ قُلْ هِيَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾ by right, even if others share them with them, ﴿خَالِصَةً﴾ exclusively theirs — in the nominative and the accusative [خَالِصَةٌ]; [the accusative is] a ḥāl (circumstantial) — ﴿يَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ كَذَلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ الْآيَاتِ﴾ We make them clear, like that making clear, ﴿لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ who reflect, for they are the ones who benefit from them.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ رَبِّيَ الْفَوَاحِشَ﴾ the major sins, such as fornication, ﴿مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ﴾ i.e. their open and their secret [forms], ﴿وَالْإِثْمَ﴾ disobedience, ﴿وَالْبَغْيَ﴾ against people ﴿بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ﴾ which is wrongdoing, ﴿وَأَنْ تُشْرِكُوا بِاللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِ﴾ for associating it ﴿سُلْطَانًا﴾ any proof, ﴿وَأَنْ تَقُولُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ such as forbidding what has not been forbidden, and other things.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلٌ﴾ a term; ﴿فَإِذَا جَاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ لَا يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ﴾ from it ﴿سَاعَةً وَلَا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ﴾ before it.

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿يَا بَنِي آدَمَ إِمَّا﴾ in it the nūn of the conditional إِنْ is assimilated (idghām) into the added (mazīda) مَا; ﴿يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِنْكُمْ يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آيَاتِي فَمَنِ اتَّقَى﴾ associating partners ﴿وَأَصْلَحَ﴾ his deeds, ﴿فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ in the Hereafter.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾ were too proud ﴿عَنْهَا﴾ and did not believe in them, ﴿أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿فَمَنْ﴾ i.e. no one ﴿أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ by ascribing a partner and a child to Him, ﴿أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِآيَاتِهِ﴾ the Qur'an? ﴿أُولَئِكَ يَنَالُهُمْ﴾ will reach them ﴿نَصِيبُهُمْ﴾ their portion ﴿مِنَ الْكِتَابِ﴾ of what was written for them in the Preserved Tablet, of provision, term of life and other things, ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُنَا﴾ i.e. the angels, ﴿يَتَوَفَّوْنَهُمْ قَالُوا﴾ to them, by way of reproach: ﴿أَيْنَ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَدْعُونَ﴾ worship ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ قَالُوا ضَلُّوا﴾ they have vanished ﴿عَنَّا﴾ and we do not see them; ﴿وَشَهِدُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ at death ﴿أَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا كَافِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ the Exalted to them on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿ادْخُلُوا فِي﴾ the company of ﴿أُمَمٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ فِي﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) ادْخُلُوا ﴿النَّارِ كُلَّمَا دَخَلَتْ﴾ the Fire ﴿أُمَّةٌ لَعَنَتْ أُخْتَهَا﴾ the one before it, for having gone astray through it, ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا ادَّارَكُوا﴾ caught up with one another ﴿فِيهَا جَمِيعًا قَالَتْ أُخْرَاهُمْ﴾ they are the followers, ﴿لِأُولَاهُمْ﴾ i.e. for their eminent ones [Translator's note: so vocalized in the source, لِأَجْلَائِهِمْ; the sense may be لِأَجْلِهِمْ, "concerning them"], and they are the ones followed: ﴿رَبَّنَا هَؤُلَاءِ أَضَلُّونَا فَآتِهِمْ عَذَابًا ضِعْفًا﴾ doubled ﴿مِنَ النَّارِ قَالَ﴾ the Exalted: ﴿لِكُلٍّ﴾ of you and of them ﴿ضِعْفٌ﴾ a doubled punishment, ﴿وَلَكِنْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ [تَعْلَمُونَ], what each group has.

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿وَقَالَتْ أُولَاهُمْ لِأُخْرَاهُمْ فَمَا كَانَ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا مِنْ فَضْلٍ﴾ because you did not disbelieve on our account, so we and you are equal. The Exalted says to them: ﴿فَذُوقُوا الْعَذَابَ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْسِبُونَ﴾

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾ were too proud ﴿عَنْهَا﴾ and did not believe in them, ﴿لَا تُفَتَّحُ لَهُمْ أَبْوَابُ السَّمَاءِ﴾ when their souls are taken up to it after death, and they are brought down to Sijjīn — unlike the believer, for whom they are opened and whose soul is taken up to the seventh heaven, as has come in a hadith — ﴿وَلَا يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ حَتَّى يَلِجَ﴾ enters ﴿الْجَمَلُ فِي سَمِّ الْخِيَاطِ﴾ the eye of the needle, which is impossible, and so is their entering. ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ [with this] recompense ﴿نَجْزِي الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ through disbelief.
